subject: Customer keystore egress limits, operator access, and subprocessor notice
messages:
From: Lisa Gonzales <lisa.gonzales@healthcore.com>
To: dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: security@healthcore.com; procurement@healthcore.com
Date: Fri, 05 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood private deploy — keystore, operator limits, subprocessors

Dylan,

Thanks for the demo yesterday. A few follow-ups from our side as we get procurement and security aligned:

- We need to confirm that HealthCore can enforce egress limits on any key material (BYOK) — i.e., the key must never leave our HSM or KMS boundary and any request that would export key material should be blocked by policy.
- Clarify the operator access model for on-prem packaged deployments: what access does Redwood ops retain for debugging? What break-glass process do you propose?
- Please provide the current list of subprocessors for the private deployment package and a timeline for notification/approval before adding new ones.

Attached: a short vendor questionnaire and an outline of the controls we will need for the SOW. Can you return a proposed addendum to the DPA that captures these points? Procurement would like redlines by COB Monday.

Lisa
Lisa Gonzales
Director, IT Security
HealthCore Labs

---
Attachment: healthcore-subproc-questionnaire.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Gonzales <lisa.gonzales@healthcore.com>
Cc: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Apr 2028 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood private deploy — keystore, operator limits, subprocessors

Lisa — thanks for the clear list. High-level answers up front, details and a DPA addendum attached.

1) BYOK boundary: Redwood’s Private (VPC/on-prem) option supports customer-controlled keys where the customer retains sole custody of the key material; our runtime can be configured to use the customer KMS endpoint so keys are not exported. We will document the technical configuration (KMS plug-in, trust certificate thumbprints, and network ACLs) in the deployment annex.

2) Operator access: by default, Redwood operators do not have access to customer key material. For debugging we offer a documented break-glass process that requires: dual approval (customer security + Redwood SRE lead), time-limited ephemeral access, and SIEM/audit events shipped to the customer. We can include an operator entitlements matrix in the addendum.

3) Subprocessors: attached is the current subprocessor list for Private packages; any changes are subject to 30-day notice and approval for enterprise customers under contract. If HealthCore requires additional controls (e.g., onshore-only subprocessors) we can add a contractual clause.

I’ve attached a draft DPA addendum that captures the above. Irene and Kim — can you review the addendum for any gaps (esp. around forensics, log retention scope, and egress policy enforcement)?

Best,
Dylan
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Apr 2028 12:36:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood private deploy — keystore, operator limits, subprocessors

Looping in some legal/controls notes. I reviewed the draft addendum — overall good, but flags below: 

- Add explicit language: "Key material SHALL NOT be exported by Redwood personnel, agents, or subprocessors; any export attempts will be logged and rejected." Use SHALL to be clear.
- Break-glass: require customer-signed authorization (SAML assertion or signed ticket) and limit to attacker forensics scope; log streaming must include session recordings and elevated auth events.
- Subprocessors: clarify the notification window and whether HealthCore has an objection right or only a right to terminate for cause. HealthCore asked for approval; we should propose a 14-day review window instead of 30, but include an exception path for emergency patches.

Kim — can you validate the SIEM fields and the retention timeframe to ensure they match our platform defaults? I will prepare legal-friendly text for the egress and operator sections.

Irene
Head of Privacy & Legal, Redwood Inference
From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 06 Apr 2028 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood private deploy — keystore, operator limits, subprocessors

Irene / Dylan — quick notes from the controls side: 

- SIEM / Audit: we can include session start/stop, command audit, and key-op events (Encrypt/Decrypt/Sign) forwarded to HealthCore’s collector. Default retention is 90 days in the platform; we can offer 365 days as an enterprise add-on.
- Egress enforcement: we have a runtime policy engine that can enforce "no-export" at the KMS client layer; when configured it rejects any operation that would return raw key material or key-wrapping tokens. We will surface failure reasons in the audit stream.
- Operator debugging: recommend a 4-hour max ephemeral window with MFA and just-in-time role elevation; break-glass requests will be tracked via the ticketing link in the addendum.

I can update the appendix with the exact SIEM field names and retention options.

Kim
Director, Platform Security
From: Lisa Gonzales <lisa.gonzales@healthcore.com>
To: dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: security@healthcore.com; procurement@healthcore.com
Date: Mon, 07 Apr 2028 16:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood private deploy — keystore, operator limits, subprocessors

Dylan / Irene / Kim — thank you, that is much clearer. A couple of follow-ups before we circulate to execs: 

- Can you add explicit language that HealthCore will be notified within 48 hours of any attempted or successful key-export attempts (even if blocked) and receive the associated audit package?
- For subprocessors: HealthCore requires an onshore-only option for any components touching key material. Is that feasible, and what delta in pricing/lead time would we expect?
- Please include the ticketing link and the exact approval flow for break-glass in the addendum so procurement can sign off.

If you can update the addendum with the 48-hour notification clause and a paragraph on the onshore-only subprocessor option, procurement will move to signature.

Lisa
